answer.generated: Parameter sharing in convolutional neural networks refers to the reuse of the same set of weights across different spatial locations within the image, which aligns with the principle of feature extraction being local and sparse. This mechanism allows the network to detect the same features regardless of their position in the image, thereby reducing the number of parameters and improving computational efficiency. By applying the same operation across different locations, the network can maintain a consistent representation of features, thus enhancing its ability to generalize across various spatial configurations within the input image.
